subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), COMPLETED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195), and CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (kb/Work PB263 + PB264). D-B's claim recorded here was that the literal's value - significand x 10^exponent - is carried EXACTLY in EVERY position through ONE rendering, NumericRenderer.LiteralNum. THAT CLAIM WAS NOT TRUE OF TWO POSITIONS WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and this row's five goldens were all VALUE-clause or arithmetic-operand positions, so none of them could have contradicted it. The CALL argument lane and the INVOKE argument lane do not reach LiteralNum at all: they render operand text through the raw EmitText.UnscaledLit helper, which returned the literal's own source text as a binary64 Real NumX for the E-form. The generated C# then handed a double to ManagedPointer<long|Int128>.Cell(...) and did not compile - conforming source rejected by a raw Roslyn CS1503 with no COBOL diagnostic at all (measured both carrier arms). UnscaledLit now honours its own scaled-integer contract for BOTH notations via TryUnscaledParts, taking the (significand, power of ten) pair exactly and never expanding it to text; the CALL lane funnels both of its non-place arms through one carrier build, and the two new goldens pin the four-cell table (two notations x BY CONTENT / BY VALUE, all four displaying the same value) plus the INVOKE arm. The evidence set now covers the argument positions the word EVERY always claimed.
